title: Google Antigravity agents prove math conjectures, rewrite AV1 decoder and design drug candidates
content:
Google's Antigravity agents tackle open problems in math, chemistry and code
Community take
36
comments
Reaction is largely skeptical, with many dismissing the post as vague marketing prose and questioning both the credit given to researchers and the legitimacy of the claimed performance numbers, though a Google researcher jumped in to clarify the results and a few commenters see genuine promise in multi-agent workflows.
Questions this post answers
What is Google's Antigravity /teamwork multi-agent system used for
It is a multi-agent system pairing Gemini 4 models with verifier agents to tackle long-standing problems in math, chemistry, and systems engineering. Examples include fully proving the 2013 Courtade-Kumar conjecture in Lean 4 (50 million lines of code), formalizing the Weil conjectures via the LEAP framework, and rewriting Google's libgav1 AV1 decoder into Rust. Developers tracking agentic AI capabilities beyond chat assistants can follow these results on daily.dev.
How much faster was Google's Rust rewrite of the libgav1 AV1 decoder compared to the original C++ version
The Rust rewrite, produced by Google's Antigravity /teamwork agents, ran 20-30% faster than the original C++ libgav1 decoder. The rewrite totaled about 170,000 lines of Rust, a result the system itself called unexpected since rewrites typically don't outperform the original. Anyone weighing a C++ to Rust migration can track real-world performance outcomes like this on daily.dev.
How can academic researchers get free access to Google's Antigravity AI system
Google is opening applications for 10,000 academic researchers and scientists to receive six months of free access to its highest usage tier for Antigravity. Access is subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection criteria. Researchers evaluating AI research tools can keep tabs on access programs like this via daily.dev.

report.summary: Google多智能体系统攻克数学猜想并重写AV1解码器
report.background: 2025年以来，AI智能体正从「聊天助手」转向可长时间自主工作的「同事」。Google的Antigravity（/teamwork）把Gemini模型与专职「验证器」智能体配对，试图让AI在数学证明、系统级代码重构、药物设计等需要长周期与高可靠性的任务上产出可验证成果。此前DeepMind的AlphaProof、Lean社区的形式化数学热潮，以及微软等推动的C++转Rust迁移，都为这类尝试铺了路。不过该消息发布后社区反应普遍怀疑，认为措辞像营销文案，对研究者署名与性能数字提出质疑，也有Google研究员出面澄清。
key_points: 架构核心是「生成＋验证」双角色：Gemini模型负责产出方案，验证器智能体负责检查对错，以此降低长链条任务中的幻觉与错误累积。
完整证明了2013年提出的Courtade-Kumar猜想，并用Lean 4形式化验证，规模达5000万行代码级别；另借LEAP框架形式化Weil猜想。
把Google自家的libgav1 AV1解码器从C++重写为约17万行Rust，运行速度快20-30%，系统自身称「重写反而更快」属意外结果。
在化学领域用于设计候选药物分子，说明同一套多智能体流程可跨数学、代码、生物医药迁移。
Google开放1万个学术研究者名额，提供6个月最高配额的免费Antigravity使用权，需符合资格与筛选条件。
report.impact: 对AI行业，这是「智能体能否产出可验证硬成果」的一次高压测试，若数字站得住，竞争焦点将从模型分数转向验证闭环与工程流水线。对开发者，C++转Rust的自动化重写若能稳定复现20-30%性能提升，系统级迁移的成本结构会被重估，但社区对数据的质疑提醒需独立复现。对普通用户，短期无直接变化，中期可能体现为更快的视频解码、更便宜的软件维护，以及AI辅助的药物研发提速；同时「AI署名科研成果」的争议会持续。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注：Lean 4 与 Mathlib（形式化数学入门）、LEAP 形式化框架、libgav1（AV1解码器，可对比Rust重写版本）、Google Antigravity 学术免费申请通道；开发者也可用 Claude Code、OpenHands 等多智能体框架自建「生成＋验证」流水线练手。
